newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major to hold inflation "by scruff of neck".
newsitem.headline: UK's Major to hold inflation "by scruff of neck".

text.p: Prime Minister John Major vowed on Wednesday to keep a tight grip on inflation as he unveiled his manifesto for the May 1 election.

He said it would help to make Britain the best place in the world to live. Speaking at a news conference Major said his aim was to "make haves of the have-nots, to bring wealth and welfare hand in hand.
"To carry forward our plans we must keep the economy fit, lean and competitive. So we will keep inflation by the scruff of its neck."

Major, unveiling what he called the boldest and most far-reaching manifesto any party had published since 1979, tackled head on opposition Labour Party Tony Blair's claim that it was time for a change after 18 years of Conservative rule. "It is time for a change. Time for a change to the next phase of Conservative prosperity that will give everyone -- no matter who they are, where they live -- more choice and more control over their lives," Major said.
He said the manifesto, which contains 25 pledges, was a watershed and summed it up as follows.

"An enterprise economy; personal prosperity and security; wealth and welfare hand in hand; a state that does less but does it better; a United Kingdom in a Europe of nation states; these are the pillars on which the next stage of Conservatism rests," Major said.
"Our goal must be to make Britain the best place in the world to live," he concluded.
